conviction_note: Balanced evidence: the bar is low (consensus Q3 comp -1.1%, EPS $0.40 down 18% y/y, FY consensus $1.93 at the bottom of the $1.90-2.00 guide) and one broker (Truist) moved its Q3 comp to +1.0%, against fuel at record highs after the July guide (diesel $6.29-6.53 in September, freight named by the CFO as a second-half margin headwind) and a strong El Nino warm-winter outlook for Q4 seasonal; the findings net to +0.5 and p_up 52 on a 7.5% absolute move gives +0.3. The skew already pays for upside (-6.76, put/call OI 0.14), so the upside half is partly in the price.
bar: Q3 revenue $3.81B (+2.4% y/y) and adjusted EPS $0.40-0.4046 from two agreeing sources (Zacks via TradingView 2026-10, https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:1a4fbcde0094b:0-tractor-supply-gears-up-for-q3-earnings-what-awaits-the-stock/ ; MarketBeat 2026-10-15, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-tractor-supply-tsco-projected-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday-2026-10-15/). Q3 comp consensus -1.1% from one source (Zacks key metrics, 2026-10-19, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/curious-tractor-supply-tsco-q3-121508677.html) against a year-ago +3.9%. Company guide (2026-07-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916365/000091636526000052/ex991-q22026earningsrelease.htm): FY26 net sales +2.5-3.5%, comps -1% to flat, adjusted EPS $1.90-2.00; no quarterly guide. FY EPS consensus $1.93 (MarketBeat). The stock trades on comps and the full-year guide.
positioning_check: Short interest: FINRA settlement 2026-07-15 showed about 30.0M shares short, 3.9 days to cover (prior 28.9M); Equibles shows about 5.6% of float, 2.5 days, undated (https://equibles.com/stocks/TSCO); no October settlement found. Not a crowded short. Skew -6.76 vol points (25d put minus 25d call): the market pays for upside; put/call open-interest ratio 0.14; event-implied move 7.73%. Stock 42% below its 52-week high, 11.9% above the low, 20-day run-up +0.96%, 5-day -0.43%, down about 43% over a year. Zacks Rank #4, Earnings ESP 0.0%, estimates flat over 30 days and up 1.2% (EPS) over two months per Investing.com. Insiders bought in early August (CEO $0.50M, director $0.10M). Reaction history: 5 of 7 prints down, last two large down prints were January and April 2026; the July guide cut was bought +3.27% and Q3 2025 +2.77%.

findings.finding: Truist raised its Q3 comparable-store-sales estimate to +1.0% from -1.8%, citing consumers adjusting to higher gas prices, more favourable weather and merchandise resets, and said trends improved through the quarter on a one-year basis (two-year trends slowed); the Zacks consensus comp is -1.1%, so this broker sits about 2 points above the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 comp +3.9% was bought +2.77%; Q2 2026 comp -1.5% with a guide cut was bought +3.27% because the miss was read as weather-driven; Q1 2026 comp +0.5% with a reaffirmed guide sold -11.69%. Comp beats have not reliably been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It is one broker's note. The Zacks comp consensus of -1.1% and the EPS consensus flat for 30 days show the street has not moved to it; had it done so, the comp consensus would sit near flat and EPS would have been revised up in the last month. The upside-paid skew suggests options traders have partly leaned that way.
findings.independence: Partly corroborated by Zacks naming better precipitation extending the spring season as a positive (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:1a4fbcde0094b:0-tractor-supply-gears-up-for-q3-earnings-what-awaits-the-stock/), and by management saying in July that June and July trends supported improvement. Contradicted in part by regional managers quoted in the same Investing.com piece saying diesel prices hurt store traffic.

findings.finding: The guide arithmetic leaves a low bar: first-half comps were about -0.6% (Q1 +0.5% on $3.59B, Q2 -1.5% on $4.54B), so the FY comp guide of -1% to flat implies a second half of about -1.4% to +0.6%, and the CFO's base case was 'modest sequential improvement' from Q2's -1.5%; the -1.1% Q3 consensus and the $1.93 FY EPS consensus both sit at the bottom of what the company guided to, against the toughest compare of the year (Q3 2025 comp +3.9%, July the hardest month).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the guide was cut in July 2026 the stock rose 3.27%, so a low bar met has been bought once; when a guide was reaffirmed in April 2026 on a soft quarter it fell 11.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the consensus already sits at the low end, which is the market's way of discounting the guide. What is not priced is a narrow-to-midpoint outcome; if the market expected that, FY consensus would sit near $1.95 rather than $1.93 and the comp consensus near -0.5%.
findings.independence: Q1 figures from the 2026-04-21 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916365/000091636526000020/ex991-q12026earningsrelease.htm); second-half base-case wording from the July call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tractor-supply-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-23/). Shares a document with finding 3's margin wording.

findings.finding: Retail diesel set records after the July guide (EIA: $5.967/gal week of 7 Sep, $6.285 on 14 Sep, $6.53 by 23 Sep; WTI $87.28 on 19 Aug to $107.02 on 15 Sep), while the CFO had named continued freight and fuel costs as a second-half gross-margin headwind, with more pressure in Q3 than Q4, and management had blamed spring fuel prices for May's comp miss; Q4 freight and the rural customer's fuel bill (about 40% drive pickups) both moved against the guide after it was set.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 guide cut, blamed on fuel and weather, was bought +3.27% as temporary; the January and April 2026 prints with margin and outlook disappointment sold -7.58% and -11.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: Fuel is public, but transmission to TSCO's Q4 guide is not quantified by anyone: EPS consensus has been flat for 30 days and up 1.2% over two months, which is not what a street that had cut for a September fuel spike would show. Diesel eased in October (European data), which limits it.
findings.independence: Kpler EIA digest 2026-09-23 records $6.53 diesel (https://www.kpler.com/blog/eia-digest-retail-prices-for-transportation-fuels-keep-getting-more-expensive); the CFO's freight/fuel margin warning is in the July call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tractor-supply-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-23/). Proxy: no TSCO document quantifies the effect. Against it: Truist reads consumers as adjusting to higher gas prices (finding 1).

findings.finding: NOAA's winter outlook (16 Oct 2026) calls for a very strong El Nino with above-average temperatures favoured across the Midwest, Mississippi Valley, much of the East and the northern tier, which is TSCO's core footprint for Q4 heating, pellet, outerwear and cold-weather seasonal categories that the Q4 guide depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Weather-driven misses have been treated as temporary (July 2026 +3.27%); no prior print in the baseline turned on a winter outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro forecast; whether management bakes it into Q4 commentary on the call is unknown. If priced into estimates, Q4 EPS consensus would have moved down in the last week, and no revision is reported.
findings.independence: NWS Brownsville outlook also notes a strong El Nino turning the pattern wetter (https://www.weather.gov/media/bro/climate/pdf/RGVSeptemberNovember2026Outlook.pdf). Proxy only; no company statement.

findings.finding: Drought covered 59.1% of the contiguous US by 1 Sep 2026 after a record-warm August, with Texas and Oklahoma under 30% of normal August rain; management cited southeastern drought as a Q2 headwind, so Q3 likely carried a similar drag in livestock/lawn-garden geographies even as Truist and Zacks describe weather as more favourable.
findings.why_not_priced: Weather is public; net direction for TSCO is ambiguous (drought can lift feed and water-related sales). Small by construction.
findings.independence: Q2 drought attribution: https://sgbonline.com/tractor-supply-cuts-outlook-on-q2-shortfall-absorbs-petsense-impairment-charge/ . Contradicted in part by Truist (finding 1) and Zacks citing favourable weather. Secondary aggregator source for the drought share.

findings.finding: CEO Hal Lawton bought 15,600 shares (~$0.50M at $32.15) on 4 Aug 2026 and director Andre Hawaux 3,150 shares (~$0.10M at $31.83) on 3 Aug, open-market buys after the guide cut, near today's $32.60.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy pattern in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since early August via Form 4; it is a signal about management's view of the trough rather than a number for this print, so it is mostly priced; filed small.

findings.finding: Dollar General, the closest rural-value read-through to report after TSCO's July call, posted May-July same-store sales +3.5% with traffic +2.0% and raised its FY comp guide to 2.5-2.9% on 27 Aug 2026, which argues the rural low-income consumer held up through July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of TSCO trading on DG prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and mostly consumables; TSCO's weakness is discretionary and big-ticket, so the read-through is weak and largely in the price.
findings.independence: Proxy; overlaps July only. Same DG release shows an 81bp tariff-refund gross-margin benefit (finding 8).

findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refunds were ordered for all importers of record with interest (CIT order 4 Mar 2026); Dollar General booked about 81bp of gross margin from refunds in its July quarter, and TSCO's own Q2 gross margin cited tariff-related benefits, so a Q3 refund benefit is possible, though management guided lower tariff benefits for the second half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for TSCO; lessons record refund theses splitting on guidance direction.
findings.why_not_priced: No TSCO-specific refund amount is public; it lands inside management's guided 'lower tariff benefits' language, so sized near zero.
findings.independence: DG release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000029534/000110465926101918/tm2623914d1_ex99.htm); TSCO Q2 margin language via call summaries.

findings.finding: 8-K of 7 Aug 2026: EVP and Chief Technology Officer, Digital and Pet Services Robert Mills resigned effective 7 Aug; Allivet and VIP Petcare moved to the Chief Merchandising Officer and Petsense to the Chief Stores Officer, with retention-style equity grants to both.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for 10 weeks; relevant only if pet services strategy (a stated growth pillar) is reframed on the call.

findings.finding: TSCO sold $500M of 5.200% senior notes due 2032 (priced 19 Aug, closed 25 Aug 2026) with proceeds to repay credit-line borrowings and general purposes: the money refinances revolver debt that funded buybacks and the VIP Petcare acquisition, not distress.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and routine; the only print effect is a little more interest expense, already in estimates.

outside_window.finding: Replacement long-term financial framework promised with Q4 2026 results (early 2027), not at this print.

baseline_tension: The skew pays for upside and the bar is low, so the positive half of what I found (Truist comp, low-end consensus) agrees with the options market and is partly priced; the negative half (record diesel after the guide, warm-winter outlook) cuts against the skew and rests on macro proxies, so it is sized small and the net is near zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew; short interest not crowded): fuel finding shrunk -1.5 to -1.2 and El Nino -0.5 to -0.4, because both oppose an upside-paid -6.76 skew and rest on macro transmission
Lesson 5 (proxies small): drought finding -0.5 to -0.3, given Truist and Zacks describe weather as favourable (own caveat)
Lesson 2 (one-offs as fractions, inside guidance): tariff refund +0.2 to +0.1
Lesson 1 (fact is not reaction; 5 of 7 prints sold): insider buy +0.5 to +0.4 and guide-arithmetic +0.8 to +0.7; p_up left at 52
Truist comp, Dollar General, CTO and notes findings left unchanged
